name: The Hollow Reach
subtitle: Twenty-eight hexes of borderland between the Duke's road and the wild
blurb: A river valley, a king's road that is not as safe as it was, a marsh that keeps what it takes, and a shelf of mountains with something in them. Gallows Ford is the last town; Waystone Cross is the last crossroads; past Ravenfell nobody has counted the miles in a generation.

tables.name: The road out of the Reach

entries.text: A merchant caravan out of Gallows Ford — four wagons, two guards, and a clerk who wants the news
A mounted patrol of the Duke's own, three lances, in no mood to be delayed
Footpads working the hedges — two of them, and they have not decided yet
Pilgrims bound for Waystone Cross, singing badly
Nothing but weather, and the road going on
Goblin raiders, three of them, spoiling for a fight
A wolf pack, circling at a distance and counting you
A dire boar, rooting, with a temper
Nothing — the wood holds its breath and lets you pass
A charcoal burner's camp: friendly, nervous, and glad of the company
Owlbear sign — scat, clawed bark, and a dead ox gone cold
A lizardfolk hunting party, up to their thighs in black water
Giant frogs, sunning on a mudbank — they notice you second
A cloud of stirges, drawn by the warmth
An old ferryman who asks too many questions and answers none
Nothing. The fens are very patient
Bandits in the folds of the ground, waiting for the road to empty
A hobgoblin scout party, marching in silence
Wild dogs, gone half feral since the last winter
Nothing but wind and the grass lying flat under it
A shepherd with a story, a lamb to sell, and nowhere to be

rumours: The beacon on Kestrel Crag was never lit the night the Duke's riders went east. Someone in Gallows Ford knows why.
They say the Howe of Nine opens if you sit on it until the sun is down. They also say what comes out is still wearing its ring.
There is a goblin shrine in Thornwood now, built out of a waystone someone dragged off the road. The Duke's patrols have stopped mentioning it.
Whatever is in Bittertarn has been in Bittertarn longer than the Reach has had a name. The mine floods every time they dig towards it.
The ferryman at Sallow Bend will take you across for a silver piece, or for a story he has not heard.
Nine pines on the ridge, planted in a ring. Nobody planted them. Nobody cuts them.

hexes.name: Kestrel Crag
hexes.description: A bare shoulder of rock above the road, crowned by a broken watchtower. The beacon basket is still there, tarred and dry, and has not been lit in forty years. From the top you can see the whole valley: the ford, the road east, and the smoke of every farm between here and the downs.
hexes.playerText: An old watchtower on the skyline, roofless. The beacon basket is still strung.

features.name: The dead beacon
features.text: Under the tarred brushwood in the beacon basket: a signal arrow, fletched red, and a purse of nine silver bits nobody came back for. Lighting the fire is visible from Barrowdown and the Shatterwall Gate — the garrison will come, and so will whatever else sees a flame on the crag.

hexes.name: Gallows Ford
hexes.description: Six hundred souls behind a stone wall, at the only reliable crossing of the Ash. A market on Threeday, a hired garrison of twenty who are mostly someone's sons, and a gallows on the east road that gives the town its name and its custom. The Company is known here; the innkeeper will stand a round and ask what you are doing with your summer.
hexes.playerText: Walled market town. Smoke, wet limestone, and the sound of the weir. A gallows stands on the east road, freshly painted.

hexes.name: Stonemill Fields
hexes.description: Good deep land, hedged into strips, with a working watermill on the Ash that grinds for half the valley. The miller's boy knows every ford between here and the fen and will say so at length.
hexes.playerText: Farmland and a working mill. The road is dry and the hedges are full of birds.

hexes.name: Widow's Acre
hexes.description: A farmstead burned to its footings ten years ago and never rebuilt. Weeds have taken the yard; the well is capped with a door and a stone. Nobody in Stonemill Fields will say the family's name out loud, and the hedges here are never cut.
hexes.playerText: A burned-out steading. The weeds are waist high and the well is capped.

features.name: The cellar cache
features.text: Under the capstone of the well, on a ledge three fathoms down: an oiled bundle with forty silver, a signet the owner never got to wear, and a child's shoe. The bundle was put there in a hurry by someone who meant to come back.

hexes.name: The Ninefold
hexes.description: Nine old pines on a low ridge, standing in a ring with a cleared middle, each too evenly spaced to be chance. The woodfolk leave them alone and cut their firewood elsewhere. Nothing grows inside the ring but moss.
hexes.playerText: Nine tall pines in a ring, evenly spaced. Nothing grows underneath them.

features.name: The hollow oak
features.text: A hollow in the largest pine at shoulder height, plugged with a fitted stone: six bolts of undutied silk, a ledger in code, and a boat hook. Somebody's smuggling runs through the Ninefold, and they are not finished with it.

hexes.name: The Ash Mile
hexes.description: The King's Road where it runs straight and dry along the river, walled with hedgebank on both sides. Six miles of good going, a milestone at each end, and a hedge thick enough to hide a dozen men with a grudge.
hexes.playerText: Straight, dry road between high hedges, with river noise on the left.

hexes.name: Marl Flats
hexes.description: Open grazing on heavy marl, fenced into big fields, with the horse fair at midsummer. The graziers will sell you a pony and tell you which three of their neighbours to avoid.
hexes.playerText: Open grazing land. Hundreds of horses, and a smell of hay and tar.

hexes.name: Reedmarch
hexes.description: Where the Ash slows and spreads, the road gives up and a causeway of hurdles takes over. Reed beds to the knee in summer, over the head in spring. Things live in here that the fens swallow and the fens keep.
hexes.playerText: Reed beds and standing water. A hurdle causeway, slick and narrow.

features.name: The sunken barge
features.text: Forty yards off the causeway, a flat barge under two feet of water with its mast still stepped: the Ash Maid, out of Gallows Ford, thirteen years missing, cargo still lashed under the tarpaulin. The rope holding the tarpaulin was cut, not rotted.

hexes.name: Barrowdown
hexes.description: Grassy mounds in ranks along the ridge, nine of them they can count and more under the turf. Sheep graze the flanks and the shepherds do not camp on the tops after dark. The barrow-dirt here has been dug before, badly, and more than once.
hexes.playerText: Grassy burial mounds along a ridge. The sheep avoid the tops.

features.name: The Howe of Nine
features.text: The largest mound has a dry-stone doorway in its eastern flank, exposed by the winter's rain: a passage going down, dressed stone, and air coming out of it that is colder than the day. There is a lintel carved with nine notches, and the notches are worn smooth.

hexes.name: Waystone Cross
hexes.description: The crossroads of the Reach: the King's Road east and west, the drove road north to Barrowdown, and a track south into the fens. A waystone stands at the meeting with the mileage to the capital cut into it, and a smaller hand-cut tally underneath that nobody will explain.
hexes.playerText: A crossroads with a carved waystone: four roads, and mileage cut into the stone.

hexes.name: Thornwood
hexes.description: Second-growth wood, thick as a hedge, cut over twice and come back angry. The road runs through it for six miles with nothing between the hedges but shadow. The Duke's patrols used to clear it every spring; this year they did not.
hexes.playerText: Close, dark second-growth wood. The road is a tunnel through it.

features.name: The goblin shrine
features.text: In a clearing a mile off the road: a waystone dragged here and stood on end, hung with iron, rags and the skulls of dogs, and fresh offerings at its foot. It was a Duke's milestone two summers ago. There are sentries, and they are bad at it.

hexes.name: Blackfen
hexes.description: Black water under willow, in channels that move when you are not looking. The fens take a beast a year and a person a decade, and the channels have been sounded by men who never came back to draw the map.
hexes.playerText: Black water and willow. The ground is not where it looks.

features.name: The lizard lair
features.text: A dry island in the middle of the fen, made of mud and bone, with a dozen lizardfolk on it and a pen of prisoners at the back. The causeway to it is under water at high water and bare for four hours either side of low.

hexes.name: The Shatterwall
hexes.description: The cliff edge of the shelf, four hundred feet of broken rock running north to south, and one switchback track up it that a loaded mule can manage. Everything east of here is higher, colder, and less asked about.
hexes.playerText: A wall of broken cliff. One switchback track climbs it, and it is not wide.

hexes.name: Shatterwall Gate
hexes.description: A toll post and a watchtower at the foot of the climb, with a chain across the road and a corporal who wants two bits a head and a good reason. The last garrison but one is buried at the back; the corporal will tell you about it if you buy him a cup.
hexes.playerText: A toll chain and a watchtower. Two bits a head, and the corporal counts carefully.

hexes.name: The Weeping Wood
hexes.description: Birches on wet ground, with water standing between them and the bark white enough to walk by at dusk. Something hangs from the biggest tree at the meeting of two rides; the woodfolk say it has hung there a long time and mean to leave it.
hexes.playerText: White birches on wet ground. Something hangs from a tree where two rides meet.

features.name: The warning tree
features.text: A deserter in a Duke's coat, in irons, long dead, with a board nailed under him: THE ROAD IS NOT THE WOOD. The boards are replaced every few years by somebody who still cares about the distinction, and the irons have been filed at, from the inside.

hexes.name: Ashen Mere
hexes.description: A lake of black water in a bowl of hills, a mile across and cold enough to ache. Nothing fishes it. On still mornings the top of something square shows a hand's breadth under the surface, two hundred yards out from the eastern shore.
hexes.playerText: A black lake, very still. Something square under the water, well out from the shore.

features.name: The drowned chapel
features.text: A chapel roof two fathoms down, tiles intact, the bell still in its frame with the clapper taken. The altar stone is whole and the carvings on it are not the Duke's — older, and cut by somebody who knew the fen as dry land. The water came up in a year nobody in the Reach will name.

hexes.name: The Cold Shelf
hexes.description: Bare stone above the tree line, snow in the shade all summer, and a shelf road that is a mile of exposure with nothing to hold. The wind here takes sound oddly: a party can be heard a long way off, and not always by whoever was listening.
hexes.playerText: Bare stone and cold wind, above the trees. The road is a ledge.

features.name: The wyvern eyrie
features.text: A shallow cave under an overhang, floored with bone split for marrow and a long scrape of scorched rock. The occupant is out hunting most of the day and comes back at dusk with something. There are four nests; three are old.

hexes.name: The Gallowstretch
hexes.description: Where the King's Road climbs the shelf in earnest: six miles of gradient with gibbets at intervals, most empty, three not. The crows have been shot at so often they ignore the road and watch the hills instead.
hexes.playerText: A long climb with gibbets along it. Three of them are occupied.

hexes.name: Elderwood
hexes.description: Trees that were old when the Reach was new, and a floor so clear of undergrowth it reads as parkland and is not. The paths here do not follow the ground; they go where they go, and two of them go to the same place by different centuries.
hexes.playerText: Enormous old trees with a clear floor between them. The paths do not follow the contours.

features.name: The elf stairs
features.text: Thirty steps of white stone going down into the hillside, each worn in the middle to a shallow dish, ending at a door with no frame and no lock that opens on a stair going further down. The air coming up out of it is warm and smells of cut grass.

hexes.name: Fellrise
hexes.description: A long bare slope above the fen, with a cairn on the skyline that can be seen from four hexes and is walked to, still, by people who will not say why. Rain comes off the fens here and the ground is always wet.
hexes.playerText: A bare wet slope with a cairn on top that people still visit.

features.name: The chieftain's cairn
features.text: The cairn is a door, not a grave: lift the capstone and the inside is a chamber with a war-leader in it, seated, with his gear and his horses' bits and nine notches cut into the door jamb. The fens took his people; the cairn was put up by whoever was left.

hexes.name: Skarn Peak
hexes.description: An iron mine on the shelf, worked out twice and flooded twice, with the headgear still standing and the tram rails still going in. The second flooding is the one the miners talk about, because it came up from below and not from rain.
hexes.playerText: A disused mine: headgear, tram rails, and a pool of black water at the adit mouth.

features.name: The flooded level
features.text: Behind a collapsed timber in the lower level, a worked-out stope with picks left where they were dropped and a borehole in the floor, plugged with canvas and a stone, that goes down further than the mine does. The plug has been replaced recently.

hexes.name: The Long Slopes
hexes.description: Sheep pasture on the shelf, in walled intakes, with a shepherd's bothy every mile or two that is never locked and never empty of tea. The best grazing in the Reach and the most quietly defended.
hexes.playerText: Wall sheep-pasture with unlocked bothies along the wall-tops.

hexes.name: Widowwood
hexes.description: A wood that was clear-felled for the ironworks and grew back wrong: same species, wrong spacing, no birds in the middle of it. The charcoal burners work the edges and will not work the middle, which is the only thing they agree about with the miners.
hexes.playerText: Regrown woodland with no birds in the middle of it. The burners keep to the edges.

hexes.name: The Ember Plains
hexes.description: Grassland burned two summers back and burned badly: black soil, new growth coming through, and a burnt wagon train still standing where the fire caught it, on the track that was the road before the road was moved.
hexes.playerText: Burnt grassland, greening at the edges, with a burnt wagon train still on the old track.

features.name: The burnt train
features.text: Six wagons, fired from the front and the back both, with the oxen still in their yokes and the lead driver still holding the reins. Nothing was looted: the bales were slashed and left, and the strongbox was opened with a key.

hexes.name: Bittertarn
hexes.description: A mountain tarn under the north face, black and cold and round, with no inlet and no outlet that anyone has found. Nothing lives in it that will take a hook. The miners at Skarn hear something moving under the ice in deep winter, and say it is the ice.
hexes.playerText: A round black tarn under the cliffs. No inlet, no outlet, no fish.

features.name: What is in the tarn
features.text: Something long and pale under the shelf of rock on the north side, at the depth the ice does not reach, moving slowly and not like a fish. It has been caught three times in a drag net and was not in the net when the net came up.

hexes.name: Ravenfell
hexes.description: The east gate of the Reach: a ruined watchfort on the pass, abandoned the year the beacon on Kestrel Crag should have been lit, with the gate still barred from the inside and nobody's account of who barred it. Past it the road becomes a track and the miles stop being counted.
hexes.playerText: A ruined fort on the pass, gate barred from the inside. Beyond it, the road stops being a road.

hexes.name: The Kindly Fells
hexes.description: Soft hills, good water, and a hermit who has lived in the same cave for so long that the drovers leave things at the mouth of it and take away whatever he has carved in exchange. He will tell you the weather, the road, and one true thing, in that order.
hexes.playerText: Soft green hills with good water, and a cave with a hermit in it.

features.name: The hermit of Fell End
features.text: An old man in a cave with forty years of carvings on the walls, most of them of the same face. He was the corporal at Shatterwall Gate the night the beacon did not burn, and he has been walking his post in here ever since.

hexes.name: Sallow Bend
hexes.description: The last steading before the wilds: one family, a ferry across the Ash, and a standing offer of a bed for a traveller who will help with the morning's work. The ferryman takes a silver piece or a story he has not heard, and counts the second as the better fare.
hexes.playerText: One steading and a ferry. A bed for a hand with the morning's work.
